perspective:
Brandon’s available information:

- I am Brandon Talayumptewa, an Alaska Native insurance agent with a bachelor’s degree. I know I can be cautious and detail-oriented, and I sometimes worry about being too caught up in details.
- I first met Benjamin Erickson when he sought business insurance advice. I understood he was an entrepreneur/business owner and was aware he had limited formal education, so I was concerned about explaining complex insurance clearly.
- In our first meeting, Benjamin told me he wanted comprehensive coverage but some terms were new. I explained liability insurance as a safety net, gave the slip-and-fall example, and explained asset protection covers inventory/equipment. Benjamin asked for an example, asked about assets, said my explanations simplified things, and thanked me.
- In our second meeting, I had revised my belief about Benjamin’s ability to understand detailed information and felt more confident. Benjamin said he had been reading up. I explained business interruption insurance and property insurance, including damage and theft. Benjamin said these sounded crucial and reassuring.
- At our casual lunch, I felt insecure about how Benjamin perceived my cautious nature and tried to balance detail with a lighter delivery. Benjamin said he appreciates my thoroughness but also enjoys lighter moments. I told the taste-buds insurance joke. Benjamin responded with interest and said it made sense given the stakes. I connected it to assessing risks for his business.
- Later, pleased by Benjamin’s positive response, I decided to offer support beyond insurance. I suggested strategic investments and security upgrades could lower premiums and protect assets. Benjamin said my insights were invaluable, that he hadn’t considered it, called it smart/win-win, and agreed to explore it.
- Then, encouraged by our rapport and mutual benefits, I proposed a joint venture: co-developing a platform integrating risk management with financial planning for entrepreneurs. Benjamin agreed, called it groundbreaking, said our combined expertise could set us apart, and agreed to draft initial plans.
- I have access only to what I observed, what Benjamin said or shared, and my own thoughts and actions—not Benjamin’s private thoughts or narrator-only details.
